knifeSkillsGuide.title: Knife Skills - An Illustrated Kitchen Guide
knifeSkillsGuide.author: Bill Collins
knifeSkillsGuide.description: Master the fundamentals of knife selection, grip, and cutting techniques
knifeSkillsGuide.introduction: Proper knife skills are the foundation of efficient, safe, and professional cooking. This guide covers knife types, sharpening, gripping, and all essential cutting techniques.

knifeTypes.name: Chef's Knife
knifeTypes.technique: Rock motion - tip stays on board, handle rises and falls
knifeTypes.safetyTip: Curl fingers into claw position when holding food

knifeTypes.name: Paring Knife
knifeTypes.technique: Held like a pencil, controlled cuts
knifeTypes.safetyTip: Keep thumb behind blade, away from cutting edge

knifeTypes.name: Serrated Bread Knife
knifeTypes.technique: Sawing motion - never apply downward pressure alone
knifeTypes.safetyTip: Serrated blades are sharp - handle carefully

knifeTypes.name: Boning Knife
knifeTypes.safetyTip: Sharp blade requires respect - careful thumb placement

knifeTypes.name: Utility Knife
knifeTypes.usage: General cutting, between chef's and paring

grips.name: Chef's Grip (Proper Grip)
steps: Hold knife handle with three fingers: index, middle, and ring
Rest pinky and thumb under the handle
Keep wrist straight, not bent
Let blade rest on middle knuckle
Index and middle fingers behind blade, ready to control

grips.name: Claw Grip (Food Holding)
grips.description: How to safely hold food being cut
steps: Curl fingers of food-holding hand into a claw
Knuckles face the blade
Thumb tucked behind fingers
Fingertips point downward, not exposed
Move fingers back as you cut (advance the claw)

grips.name: Pinch Grip
grips.description: For paring knife and detailed work
steps: Pinch the blade between thumb and index finger
Other fingers curl around handle
Blade stays low to board
Use for controlled, precise cuts

cuttingTechniques.name: Dice
steps: Cut vegetable into planks/slices of desired thickness
Stack slices and cut into batons (sticks)
Turn batons and cut across to create cubes
Smaller stacks for smaller dice
cuttingTechniques.technique: Let knife do the work - smooth cutting motion

cuttingTechniques.name: Julienne
cuttingTechniques.size: 1/8 inch x 1/8 inch x 2-3 inches long
steps: Square off the vegetable first (remove rounded sides)
Cut into thin planks
Stack planks and cut into sticks
All sticks should be uniform length

cuttingTechniques.name: Brunoise
steps: Similar to dice but with thinner starting slices
Results in very small, perfect cubes
Requires precision and practice
Usually done with medium-sized vegetables
cuttingTechniques.technique: Precision is more important than speed

cuttingTechniques.name: Slice
steps: Hold vegetable or meat firmly
Cut perpendicular to the length
Use rocking motion for vegetables
Use smooth slicing motion for meat
cuttingTechniques.technique: Cut against the grain for meat

cuttingTechniques.name: Mince
steps: Roughly chop the ingredient first
Gather into a pile
Rock the knife over it repeatedly
Continue until desired fineness

cuttingTechniques.name: Chop
steps: Use rocking or chopping motion
Size doesn't need to be uniform
Faster than precise cuts
For ingredients that will be blended or cooked down
cuttingTechniques.technique: Let the knife's weight do the work

steps: Hold honing steel vertical (tip down on board)
Place knife heel against steel at 15-20 degree angle
Draw knife down and back in one smooth motion
Repeat 5-10 times on each side
Alternate sides with each stroke

sharpening.frequency: Every few months or when needed
steps: Soak whetstone 10-15 minutes
Place on towel to prevent slipping
Start with coarse side if dull
Place blade at 15-20 degree angle
Draw knife diagonally across stone (heel to tip)
Flip and repeat on other side
End with fine-grit side for polishing
sharpening.result: Sharp blade ready for precise cutting

steps: Use professional sharpening service
Or electric knife sharpener at home
Professional services preserve blade life

safetySummary: Always use a sharp knife - dull knives require more pressure and are more likely to slip
Use the claw grip to protect your fingers
Keep your wrist straight, not bent
Let the knife do the work - don't force cuts
Cut away from your body and others
Focus on the task - no distractions
Never leave knives loose in a sink
Use a cutting board - never cut on glass or stone
Hone your knife before each use for optimal performance
